Q1
Is this one process with three rounds (06/24, 07/25, 09/11/2013) and a round-0 bucket for the 04/08 contact and 06/21 Party A proposal?
Yes. One process. Round 1 = 06/24 outreach decision; round 2 = 07/25 selection of four for staged diligence; round 3 = 09/11 request for final indications; signing ends round 3.

Gap with no reported acquirer contact of about two months or more: 04/08/2013 (BofA call to Party A, p. 27) to 06/21/2013 (Party A proposal, p. 30). E5 tests: (a) fails, since Party A was kept in view (May 9 report, June 24 plan to approach Party A, pp. 27, 31); (b) fails, 74 days with no reported end; (c) met by the 06/24 decision. Alternative boundary: no supported alternative. E6 makes the first request for final indications (09/11) a new round even with the same four bidders, and 07/25 changed both the set and the stage.

No supported alternative boundary, so no rows move. Formality follows E11, not the round numeral: the 09/18 and 09/21 bids answer the final-indications request (E11 rule 2) whatever the round is numbered; the counterfactual on that reading is in Q9.
Q2
How should Party A be treated before its 08/05 NDA, and does its 09/18 reiteration earn a Bid row?

Party A enters with its round-0 bid (#8) and is listed in round 1 as 'still being received, not admitted' (no NDA or package). Its 09/18 reiteration is a round-3 Bid row, Formal, because it answers the final request.

The Special Committee reviewed the June 21 proposal alongside the round-1 indications (p. 33) and admitted Party A to round 2 subject to an NDA (pp. 33–34). On 09/18 it called its range 'best and final' (p. 36). E10's 'Bid reaffirmed' does not fit, since the target was not finalizing with Party A.

Dropping #39 would leave Party A with no round-3 submission and make its exit read as a non-submitter's. Treating it as admitted to round 1 would add it to the round-1 admitted set (three named signers plus an unknown number of the 16 unnamed, Q5).
Q3
Did the 50 parties approached count CSC and Pamplona as one party or two?
Unresolved. Strategic remainder is 13 either way; the financial cohort is 34–35 with Count blank. Total contacted is 49–50 bidder units.

The filing says '50 parties, including CSC and Pamplona, who together we refer to as CSC/Pamplona' and splits 15 strategic / 35 financial (p. 32). Later it counts CSC/Pamplona as one strategic bidder among the 20 signers (p. 32).
Counting CSC/Pamplona as one party would make #12 exactly 35 and allow Count = 35.
Q4
What was the outcome of the round-1 due date of 07/23/2013?
Late bids accepted.

CSC/Pamplona bid on 07/23. Party B (07/24) and Party C (oral 07/24) bid after the due date, and both were reviewed and advanced on 07/25 (p. 33). Party C's written revision (#26) came later on 07/25, after the meeting (p. 34). It is placed in round 1 because it answers the round-1 request.
If the one-day lag is read as within tolerance, the outcome would be Enforced. #26 could instead be placed in round 2.
Q5
When did the 16 unnamed financial NDA signers sign and leave, and were they eligible for the 07/23 due date?

Unresolved timing. Account for the cohort once by an inferred Dropped by target by 09/11/2013 (#37), the first transition by which all 16 are established as out; leave individual signing dates, 07/23 eligibility and actual exit dates unknown.

The 20 NDAs were signed 'over the next two months' (p. 32); only Party B, Party C, CSC/Pamplona and Party A are dated, and Party A's 08/05 NDA shows signing continued after 07/23. Three round-1 indications and Party A's June 21 proposal were reviewed on 07/25 (p. 33); the 07/25, 08/27 and 09/11 requests name only the four (pp. 34–36).

With signing dates, members eligible at 07/23 would take Did not submit by 07/23, other signers by 07/25 Dropped by target at the selection (#25), and later signers an exit at 08/27 or 09/11; the round-1 admitted count (three named plus up to 16) would become exact.
Q6

Late bids accepted.
CSC/Pamplona and Party B submitted on 09/09. Party A and Party C submitted on 09/10 (p. 35), and all four were reviewed on 09/11 and invited to the final round (pp. 35–36).
Enforced if a one-day lag is ignored. The rest of the map is unchanged.
Q7
Should CSC/Pamplona's bids that carried a two-week exclusivity request be Conditions = Heavy despite fully committed Pamplona financing?
Heavy, applying E12's rule that a stated multi-week or exclusive period counts as further substantive diligence. Confirmatory diligence did follow under exclusivity (p. 38).

Each bid asked for two weeks of exclusive negotiations (pp. 35–37), and Pamplona committed 100% of the capital. What followed during exclusivity was described as confirmatory diligence and documentation (pp. 38–39).
Light would mark the winner's offers as near-firm, raising its measured commitment relative to Party A and Party B (Heavy or Unclear).
Q8
What was the outcome of the round-3 due date of 09/18/2013?
Enforced.

CSC/Pamplona, Party A and Party B responded on 09/18, and Party C did not (p. 36). The Special Committee acted on the bids in hand on 09/19, choosing CSC/Pamplona and setting a $21.25 price requirement (pp. 36–37).
None likely. Passed without action would only fit if the 09/21 counter-offer were read as continued bidding.
Q9
Are the 09/18 and 09/21 bids Formal because they answered a final solicitation?
Formal (E11 rule 2), with conditions recorded separately.

BofA asked for 'final indications of interest by September 18', with exclusivity for one bidder to follow (p. 36). Party A called its bid 'best and final', and CSC/Pamplona's $21.25 was a 'last and best offer' (pp. 36–37). During finalization Kirkland, CSC/Pamplona's counsel, returned a revised merger-agreement draft on 10/07 (p. 39).

If 'final indications' were not a genuine final solicitation, #38, #39, #40 and #44 would be Informal. CSC/Pamplona's standing $21.25 (#44) would then need a Formal Bid reaffirmed row at 10/07/2013, carried from #44, for Kirkland's returned markup (E10, E11); Party A and Party B would have no Formal bid. Under the current map #44 is already Formal in a final round, so no reaffirmation row is added.

BofA Merrill Lynch (Merrill Lynch, Pierce, Fenner & Smith Incorporated)

After Party A was sounded out in April 2013, Mac-Gray's board hired BofA Merrill Lynch and, on 06/24/2013, had its Special Committee approach 50 parties. Twenty signed NDAs, but only CSC/Pamplona, Party B and Party C gave preliminary indications, alongside Party A's unsolicited $17–$19 proposal of 06/21. The Committee advanced those four to a staged-diligence round, in which strategic bidders saw less customer data, and then asked for final indications by 09/18. CSC/Pamplona bid $20.75 with fully committed Pamplona funding, Party B offered a $21.50 package including options, Party A stood at $18–$19, and Party C dropped out. The Committee chose CSC/Pamplona, obtained $21.25 in exchange for two weeks of exclusivity (later extended), and signed on 10/14/2013.
